claims.text: The driver's own chat message asks the rider to cancel: 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side' (MSG-02733-001, sent 2026-08-15T07:52:21+08:00). Under POL-NS-10(f), a rider's own cancellation is refunded in full where the record shows the driver asked the rider to cancel. The rider's reply 'ok cancelling' (MSG-02733-002) is the direct consequence of that request, and the cancellation was recorded at 07:55:21, three minutes later.

The trip record confirms the cancellation was recorded under reason code RIDER_CANCELLED and cancelled_by RIDER, with no boarding event and no driver termination for a no-show. POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. None of those codes appears; the record shows RIDER_CANCELLED. Limb (d) therefore fails and the no-show fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

The driver never arrived at the pickup point. The GPS trace shows 49 driver fixes but zero qualifying in-geofence fixes: qualifying_fix_count is 0 and longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec is 0.0 against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m. The driver's minimum distance from the pin across the whole trace is 7000.03 m, and his speeds run 57.2 to 62.9 kph throughout — he was on an expressway, not at the pickup. POL-NS-02 requires at least 3 consecutive in-radius fixes at 25 m accuracy or better; there are none, so the driver never arrived and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails.

Even on the arrival marker's own terms the waiting clock was never served. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 180 second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180). POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full where the effective dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, whether or not the rider was present. The shortfall is the full 180 seconds.

The driver's arrival marker is false. The trip record carries arrival_marker BUTTON and no 'arrived' event at all — arrived_at is null and the events list runs driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled with no arrival step. POL-NS-05 treats an arrival marker as false where the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 kph or above; the driver's minimum distance is 7000.03 m and his speeds are 57.2 to 62.9 kph. No qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, so under POL-NS-05(ii) the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the referrals list.

The rider was at the pickup point and coordinating. The rider track places the rider's device 16.26 m from the pin — well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius — and the rider's only message 'ok cancelling' was sent in direct response to the driver's request. The rider did everything the platform asks: she was at the pin and she answered the driver.

The fare ledger shows the $4.50 cancellation fee was charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and that the fee line reconciles to the platform figure of $4.50, so the amount contested is the cancellation-fee line and nothing else. POL-NS-06 directs that the cancellation-fee line be refunded; no booking or platform fee is in issue on this cancelled trip.

The driver's own profile shows a prior no-show flag and a prior deviation flag, but I do not rely on those: POL-GEN-01 makes prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags lifetime counters that are context only and may never ground a finding. I note them solely so the record is complete, and I rest the rider's case on the trip's own evidence.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING — no advisory covers Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3 in this window. Under POL-NS-06(i) a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the dwell-accumulation limb unavailable, so the driver cannot use a kerb restriction or enforcement operation to sum separate in-geofence intervals. The absence is itself citable and it removes the only counter the driver side has to the shortfall.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the $4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02733 is refunded in full to the rider, and no money is paid to the driver.

THE FEE. The rider cancelled the trip herself at 07:55:21 (EV-TRIP-02733: cancelled_by RIDER, cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED). That is 420 seconds after the 07:48:21 match, so the 180-second grace in POL-NS-10(a) does not by itself make the cancellation free. But POL-NS-10(f) refunds a rider's own cancellation in full where the record shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and it does here. The chat log EV-CHAT-02733 (weight 1.0) carries the driver's message MSG-02733-001 sent 07:52:21, read 07:52:51 — 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side' — answered by the rider's MSG-02733-002 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21. The fare breakdown EV-FARE-02733 (weight 1.0) shows the cancellation-fee line of $4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The amount refunded is therefore $4.50, the whole contested amount.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. None is payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full (or POL-NS-10(g) applies). Neither holds. The trip was terminated by the rider, not by the driver under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, so POL-NS-01(d) fails on the face of the record; and POL-NS-10(g) needs the rider to cancel after the driver had arrived under POL-NS-02 with the free waiting period already served. That did not happen: EV-GPS-02733 shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup pin was about 7,000 m, at 57–63 km/h throughout, with zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds.

ON THE CLAIMS. Both sides' claims that POL-NS-01(d) fails, that no admissible arrival exists under POL-NS-02, that the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period, and that the $4.50 line is the only amount in issue are accepted as to their facts (no arrival marker was ever recorded — arrived_at is null — and the trace never enters the 50 m STANDARD radius). They point the same way as the ruling; the decisive clause on these facts is POL-NS-10(f), because the fee was triggered by the rider's own cancellation, so POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 are supporting rather than governing.

NO FALSE-ARRIVAL REFERRAL. I reject the request, made by both sides, for a POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral. POL-NS-05 fires only where the trip record carries an 'arrived' event whose timestamp the GPS trace contradicts. TRP-02733 records no arrival event at all and arrival_marker is BUTTON, so there is no false marker and the clause produces no referral; nothing is added to the referrals list. The driver's request that the rider cancel while he was still about 7 km away is a driver-quality question the platform may wish to look at through its own processes, but no clause in force directs a referral for it.

POL-NS-04. The rider's only message, 'ok cancelling', is a response to the driver's request, not a locating or coordinating message within POL-NS-04(a), so that clause does not independently exonerate her; the refund does not depend on it.

DISCARDED CLAIMS. The two claims about the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02733-01 were discarded by the referee because the artifact is MISSING and they did not name its issue code — it is at weight 0.0, it carries no fact, and nothing in this ruling rests on it. The claim citing prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags was discarded because POL-GEN-01 makes those lifetime counters context only. No artifact below weight 1.0 carries any deciding fact.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts are carried by the chat log, the trip record and the fare breakdown, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect, $4.50, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00 and may execute automatically.

POL-NS-10(f) refunds a rider's own post-grace cancellation in full where the record shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and that is exactly what this record shows. The fee also fails independently as a no-show charge: POL-NS-01 limb (d) needs termination by the driver under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, but the trip record (EV-TRIP-02733) shows cancelled_by RIDER with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED; POL-NS-02 is not satisfied because the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02733) contains 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes, a minimum distance of 7,000.03 m from the pin and speeds of 57.2-62.9 kph, so the driver never arrived (limb (b) fails); and POL-NS-06 is not satisfied because the in-geofence dwell was 0 s against the 180 s free waiting period in force. The fee line is $4.50 (EV-FARE-02733: total_charged 4.50, cancellation_fee 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), which is the whole contested amount.

To the driver: no compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not — limbs (b), (c) and (d) all fail. POL-NS-03 does not help either, because your fixes lie about 7,000 m from the pin, far beyond its 400 m ceiling, so this is a never-arrived case, not a wrong-entrance one. The false-arrival referral both sides asked for under POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire: POL-NS-05 operates on a trip_record 'arrived' event, and this record carries none at all (arrived_at is null; the events are driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), so there is no marker to test and no false-arrival entry to add to referrals. The rider's POL-NS-04 claim does not carry her either — her only message, 'ok cancelling', is not locating or coordinating content (limb (a) fails) and her single rider-track fix is timestamped 07:57:11, after the 07:55:21 cancellation (limb (c) fails) — but that changes nothing, since POL-NS-10(f) already requires the full refund.

ruling.explanation:
The $4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full.

Rider — your account is supported. You cancelled only because the driver asked you to: the in-app chat (EV-CHAT-02733, weight 1.0) shows the driver writing at 07:52:21 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side', you replying 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21, and the cancellation being recorded at 07:55:21. POL-NS-10(f) makes a rider's own cancellation chargeable after the 180-second post-match grace (accepted 07:48:21, cancelled 07:55:21, grace_after_match_sec 180), BUT it must be refunded in full where the record shows the driver asked the rider to cancel. That exception is met on the face of the chat log, so the fee line on EV-FARE-02733 ($4.50; total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is returned in full.

Driver — the record does not support keeping the fee, and two no-show anchors fail independently. POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails: your GPS track (EV-GPS-02733, weight 1.0) never places you inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes, and your closest approach to the pin across the entire trace is 7,000.03 m while travelling at 57.2–62.9 km/h. POL-NS-01 limb (d) fails: the trip was terminated by the rider under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED, not by you under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. POL-NS-06 gives the same answer independently: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period in force (platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a 180-second shortfall, so the fee is refunded whether or not the rider was present. POL-NS-10(g), which would have preserved the fee after a completed wait, cannot apply because you never arrived.

The claims that POL-NS-05 should record a false-arrival event are rejected. POL-NS-05 fires only on a false 'arrived' event, and this trip record carries none (arrived_at is null; the events list runs driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), so no false-arrival referral arises; the refund rests on POL-NS-10(f), not POL-NS-05(ii). The POL-NS-04 rider-presence claims are also rejected: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating rider message and 'ok cancelling' is not one, and the single rider fix in the trace is timestamped 07:57:11, after the 07:55:21 cancellation, so it cannot show presence across the waiting window — in any event the refund does not depend on POL-NS-04.

EV-ADVIS-02733-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so POL-NS-06(i) dwell accumulation is unavailable; it changes nothing because the dwell is nil. Claims resting on the lifetime profile counters prior_no_show_flags / prior_deviation_flags were discarded under POL-GEN-01 as context-only, and the two claims citing the missing advisory without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code were discarded under POL-GEN-02(1).

Confidence is 0.9, capped by the artifacts carrying the deciding fact — the chat log (EV-CHAT-02733) and the trip record (EV-TRIP-02733), both at weight_multiplier 1.0. No POL-NS-09 trigger applies: no admissible artifacts contradict on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the anti-farming counters (no_show_terminations_30d 0) and dispute counters (0 and 0) do not fire; and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. No driver compensation is payable, because POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full. The monetary effect of $4.50 is below the $8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue. No clause produces a referral on these facts.
